evidence.quote: I would say that the Committee is, is of a mind to, to raise the federal funds rate at the March meeting, assuming that conditions are appropriate for doing so.
I think there’s quite a bit of room to raise interest rates without threatening the labor market.
I'd be inclined to raise my own estimate of 2022 core PCE inflation—let’s just go with that—by a few tenths today.
inflation risks are still to the upside in the views of most FOMC participants and, certainly, in my view as well.
Now, the balance sheet is, is substantially larger than it needs to be.
The Committee also agreed to continue reducing its net asset purchases on the schedule we announced in December—bringing them to an end in early March.

parsed.rationale: The Chair signals a March liftoff, possibly faster and sooner tightening than last cycle, upside inflation risks, and a very tight labor market, alongside principles for balance sheet shrinkage. Acknowledged two-sided risks from Omicron and supply chains only modestly temper a clearly hawkish message.
